slides.title: Process Synchronization
content: Process synchronization ensures that multiple processes execute concurrently without interfering with shared resources or causing data inconsistency
It prevents race conditions by controlling access to critical sections of code where shared data is modified
It uses mechanisms like semaphores, mutexes, monitors, and barriers to coordinate execution
It improves system reliability, data integrity, and efficient resource utilization in concurrent environments

slides.title: Critical Section Problem
content: The critical section is the part of a program where shared resources are accessed and must be protected from concurrent access
A correct solution must satisfy mutual exclusion, progress, and bounded waiting conditions
Entry section requests access, critical section executes shared code, exit section releases access, and remainder section executes non-critical code
Solutions include software algorithms, hardware instructions, and OS-level synchronization tools

slides.title: Semaphores
content: A semaphore is a synchronization variable used to control access to shared resources using atomic operations wait() and signal()
Binary semaphore acts as a lock with values 0 or 1 to ensure mutual exclusion
Counting semaphore allows multiple resources to be shared using a range of values
Semaphores prevent race conditions but improper use can lead to deadlocks or starvation

slides.title: Producer Consumer Problem
content: The producer-consumer problem is a classic synchronization problem where producers add data to a shared buffer and consumers remove it
Synchronization ensures producers do not add data when the buffer is full and consumers do not remove data when empty
It uses mutex locks and condition variables for mutual exclusion and coordination
It demonstrates wait-notify mechanisms and efficient thread communication in concurrent systems

slides.title: Deadlock & Banker's Algorithm
content: Deadlock occurs when processes are stuck waiting for each other due to mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait conditions
Deadlock prevention removes one of these conditions while avoidance ensures safe states using algorithms
Banker's algorithm checks resource allocation and grants requests only if the system remains in a safe state
Deadlock detection and recovery involve identifying deadlocks and terminating processes or reallocating resources

slides.title: Starvation & Aging
content: Starvation occurs when a process is indefinitely delayed due to continuous preference for higher-priority processes
Aging is a technique that gradually increases the priority of waiting processes to prevent starvation
It ensures fairness in scheduling and improves system responsiveness
These concepts are important in priority-based scheduling and resource allocation systems
